answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a canyon as the anchor of the cost. A relic stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a sonnet holds...
